title: ER vs call pediatrician: quick guide
summary: Some symptoms need emergency care. Many others can start with a phone call.
whatsNormal:
Most day-to-day questions, spit-up, fussiness, diaper rash, sleep patterns, are best handled by your pediatrician's office or nurse line during business hours.

• Keep your clinic's after-hours number saved
• Nurse triage lines can often advise within minutes
• Urgent care can help for non-life-threatening issues when the office is closed
• Emergency departments are for true emergencies, they are always the right choice when in doubt for severe symptoms

Trust your instinct. If you think it is an emergency, it is OK to go.
watchFor: Symptoms worsening over hours: breathing, color, alertness, or feeding
Fever in a baby under 3 months, always needs prompt evaluation
Dehydration: no wet diapers, dry mouth, sunken soft spot
Injury after a fall, especially if vomiting or acting differently
callDoctorIf: Mild fever in an older infant with clear fluids and normal behavior, call for guidance
Rash without breathing difficulty, photo for nurse line often enough
Feeding or sleep questions that are not urgent
You are unsure but baby is stable, call pediatrician first; they will say if you need ER

disclaimer: Enfold provides general educational information. It does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you think your child has a medical emergency, call your local emergency number immediately.

triage.intro: Answer a few quick questions. When in doubt, seek emergency care.

green.title: Call your pediatrician
green.body: No emergency signs from your answers. Call your pediatrician's office or nurse line for guidance. Monitor closely and call back if anything changes.

yellow.title: Urgent visit today
yellow.body: Some symptoms need same-day evaluation even if not an ER emergency. Call your pediatrician now for an urgent appointment or after-hours guidance.

red.title: Go to ER now
red.body: These symptoms can be serious in young babies. Call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department. Call your pediatrician en route if you can.

breathing.question: Is your baby having trouble breathing, choking, or blue/gray lips?

fever_young.question: Is your baby under 3 months with fever 100.4°F (38°C) or higher?

responsive.question: Is your baby hard to wake, limp, having a seizure, or injured after a significant fall?

dehydration.question: Are there signs of dehydration (no wet diapers 12+ hours, sunken soft spot, no tears)?

vomit.question: Is there forceful vomiting, green (bile) vomit, or bloody vomit?
